title: Gate explainer shipping on a newcomer-usefulness check
summary: I read this as adding a mechanical newcomer-usefulness check to the explainer pipeline (xtask site, over the study's intro and glossary). The check would fail the build when the page isn't useful to a newcomer, so the failure shows up before publishing and a verifier pass can't hide it. I assumed the check is deterministic code, not a model-rated review, and that it must reject the current firstmate explainer if that explainer has the flaws the reader found.

defaults_applied.how: The gap is that nothing in the pipeline measures usefulness to a newcomer, so the fix is a gate, not a one-off rewrite of the intro.
The usefulness rule is enforced by the site build, not by prose.
Each criterion gets passing and failing fixture tests; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
One focused change in the xtask site code, with the design doc and changelog updated.
The design doc records the alternatives and why a mechanical gate was chosen.
Error messages and docs are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The explainer is the Pages site built by `cargo run -p xtask -- site` from studies/firstmate-work-handling, including intro.json.
The independent reader's 2-of-5 rating is not available in the repo, so the check targets newcomer-facing structure (undefined terms, missing orientation, id-heavy text) as a proxy.
A deterministic check is preferred over a model-rated check because the verifier can only run cargo commands and a model call isn't reproducible.
If the current firstmate intro fails the new check, fixing it in this change is acceptable but kept minimal.
question: Should the gate be purely mechanical, or should it also call a model to rate the explainer for a newcomer? I assumed purely mechanical.

acceptance_criteria.text: The explainer build code defines a newcomer-usefulness check with named, documented criteria (for example: every term used in the page is defined in the intro or glossary before its first use, the intro states what the system is and what the page lets a reader do, ids and jargon never appear without plain-language text, size limits on the intro). Each criterion has a stated reason.
The check runs inside the site build, so a page that fails it is not written or published, and the error names the failed criterion and the offending text.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`. Tests cover each criterion with a passing and a failing study fixture, and all pass.

Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site` on the repository. The result is stated: it either builds because the firstmate intro and glossary were revised to satisfy the check, or it fails with a named criterion. Any shipped explainer content passes.

docs/design/explainer-site.md records the check, the alternatives (model-rated review, human review) and why a mechanical gate was chosen. The limit is stated: it catches structural unhelpfulness, not a reader's 2-of-5 judgment.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.

out_of_scope: Rewriting the whole firstmate study or its claims.
Changing the 18 study validation rules or the study capability's verifier.
Adding a model-based reader agent to Athena's pipeline.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or CI configuration beyond what the build step already runs.
departures: Higher cost, longer runtime and lower acceptance than the reference because the request is vague on mechanism (mechanical vs. model-rated), and the change touches the site code, the design doc and possibly the study's intro content.
